hints: First impose the logarithm domains: 2x+3>0, 2x+5>0, and 3x>0.
Combine the left side as the logarithm of (2x+3)²/(2x+5), then equate arguments.
Clear the denominator, solve the resulting three-term quadratic, and reject any candidate outside the original domains.
walkthrough:
Apply the power law of logarithms to the first term:
$$2\ln(2x + 3) = \ln\left((2x + 3)^2\right)$$

Combine the two logarithmic terms on the left using the quotient rule:
$$\ln\left((2x + 3)^2\right) - \ln(2x + 5) = \ln\left(\dfrac{(2x + 3)^2}{2x + 5}\right)$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{(2x + 3)^2}{2x + 5}\right) = \ln(3x)$$

Remove logarithms by equating the positive arguments:
$$\dfrac{(2x + 3)^2}{2x + 5} = 3x$$

Multiply both sides by $(2x + 5)$ and expand:
$$(2x + 3)^2 = 3x(2x + 5)$$
$$4x^2 + 12x + 9 = 6x^2 + 15x$$

Rearrange into a three-term quadratic equation:
$$6x^2 - 4x^2 + 15x - 12x - 9 = 0$$
$$2x^2 + 3x - 9 = 0$$

Factor the quadratic equation:
$$(2x - 3)(x + 3) = 0$$
$$2x - 3 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{3}{2}$$
$$x + 3 = 0 \implies x = -3$$

Test both solutions in the original logarithmic arguments:
$$\text{For } x = -3: \quad \ln(3(-3)) = \ln(-9) \text{ is undefined for real numbers, so reject } x = -3.$$
$$\text{For } x = \dfrac{3}{2}: \quad 2x + 3 = 6 > 0, \; 2x + 5 = 8 > 0, \; 3x = \dfrac{9}{2} > 0 \quad (\text{valid})$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Logarithm laws give $(2x+3)^2=3x(2x+5)$; solving the resulting quadratic subject to the logarithm domains gives $x=3/2$.
